transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Jain (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Maya Alvarez (Verdantia Head of ML), Jordan Price (Platform Eng), Dr. Kevin Cho (CTO), Rhea Singh (Security)

Summary (auto): Walked Verdantia through Console's trace stitching, request playback, and error analysis. Covered how KV cache fallbacks appear in traces, signal surfaces for Optimize suggestions, and a proposed incident investigation playbook. Discussed SOC 2, VPC peering options, and pilot scope.

Topics: 1) Trace stitching and request correlation 2) Playback + logs 3) KV cache fallbacks 4) On-call triage playbook 5) Security artifacts and pilot plan

Transcript: 
[00:00:00] Samir: All right folks, thanks for joining. we have about 50 minutes, we'll try to run through the console flows and then leave time for Q&A. Maya, Jordan, Kevin - thanks for making time.
[00:00:18] Maya: Thanks Samir. quick note - we've been seeing a set of intermittent 500s on our recommendations endpoint, high p99 latency and sometimes the model returns truncated outputs. hoping to see how Redwood would help debug that end-to-end.
[00:00:32] Priya: Sure. the plan today is to show trace stitching in Console, how request logs tie to the model inference and KV cache layer, and then demo the request playback so you can repro the error in a safe environment.
[00:00:48] Jordan: quick context - our stack is Kubernetes in GCP, we route to a Redwood hosted inference pool, sometimes through dedicated, and we do have prefix caching at the app layer. curious how Redwood visualizes both sides.
[00:01:05] Priya: Great, that'll map well. FYI you'll hear me say 'K V cash' occasionally in the transcript, that's the ASR hiccup when I say KV cache.
[00:01:15] Dr. Kevin Cho: also, we need to make sure whatever we demo doesn't leak PHI in logs - that's a compliance hard stop.
[00:01:24] Lena: noted - we'll talk about retention and redaction settings later in the security section.
[00:01:32] Priya: jumping in — screen share: Console > Requests > Trace map. (soft typing sounds) So here you see a global timeline with each request mapped; the blue bars are inference time, green is app-side pre-processing, orange is network + marshalling.
[00:01:52] [00:01:52] Samir: One thing to call out: Console automatically stitches traces from the gateway request id, the SDK token, and any forwarded x-request-id headers. So if you have consistent IDs, it will line up.
[00:02:06] Maya: We do pass x-request-id but sometimes it's stripped by our load balancer - will that break stitching?
[00:02:12] Priya: If it's stripped, Console falls back to session heuristics: API key + timestamp proximity. It's not perfect but it catches most flows. We'll show an example.
[00:02:24] [00:02:24] Priya: here's a trace where KV cache fallback happened - see this red marker at 00:01:14? that indicates a model fallback due to cache miss and route to a larger model variant.
[00:02:38] Jordan: interesting. can you surface the exact token-level timing? we need to know if the tail latency is due to stitching or the model itself.
[00:02:46] Priya: yes - click 'token timeline' in the right pane. you'll see per-token latency and whether the runtime used a quantized kernel or fallback. sometimes the ASR will show 'quanted' instead of quantized in the export.
[00:03:00] [00:03:00] Samir: when you see KV cache misses that cause route fallback, Console shows a 'cause chain' - the original cache key, matched prefix, and the fallback variant. This is crucial for triage so you don't debug the model when it's a cache eviction issue.
[00:03:17] Maya: Nice. can the console correlate with our upstream redis evictions?
[00:03:21] Priya: We can ingest your eviction events via a webhook or Cloud Pub/Sub and annotate traces with eviction markers. We'll help set that up in the pilot.
[00:03:32] [00:03:32] Jordan: show us the request playback. we want to replay the exact request with the same headers and sample weight.
[00:03:39] Priya: opening Request Playback > select trace > click Replay. you can toggle inject-headers, toggle deterministic random seeds, and choose a sandbox model vs production. Replay runs inside a controlled tenant so it won't affect production.
[00:03:57] [00:03:57] Dr. Kevin Cho: when you replay, does it hit the same dedicated pool or a synthetic variant?
[00:04:04] Samir: By defaultReplay will target a canary sandbox that mirrors runtime kernels. for a fidelity benchmark you can opt to hit your dedicated pool but we usually recommend sampling to avoid billing surprises.
[00:04:18] [00:04:18] Maya: we need to reproduce the truncation and the 500. Where would error logs show stack traces?
[00:04:26] Priya: Error logs are in the rightmost column - you can expand request segments to see raw stderr + API error code. be aware that some low-level C++ runtime messages will be abbreviated in the transcription export.
[00:04:40] [00:04:40] Jordan: can Console show correlated application logs? we want to see our service logs alongside the request trace.
[00:04:47] Priya: Yes - we support log tailing via log forwarders (Cloud Logging, Datadog). those logs are time-aligned and appear as stitched events in the timeline.
[00:04:58] [00:04:58] Samir: also, we do token-level diffing — if two requests have similar prompts but one truncates, you can diff token-by-token to see where the model cut off.
[00:05:09] [00:05:09] Maya: that's great. How about alerting on regressions? our product team needs to be notified when p99 crosses thresholds.
[00:05:15] Priya: Console integrates with PagerDuty and Slack. We can create an alert rule on request duration, error rate, and also on 'unique truncation patterns' using our Optimize heuristics.
[00:05:29] [00:05:29] Jordan: security question - we cannot ship any raw request texts outside GCP due to PHI. can Redwood's private deployment or VPC peering help?
[00:05:38] Samir: Absolutely. for PHI workloads we recommend Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane or VPC peering and HSM/KMS. We'll share docs.
[00:05:47] [00:05:47] Rhea: And retention - how long are traces retained by default?
[00:05:51] Priya: Hosted default is 30 days, but you can configure retention per-tenant and set redaction rules for PII/PHI. In Private, retention is up to your DB.
[00:06:03] [00:06:03] Maya: could you walk through an actual failure case? I shared request id 8f7a2 earlier in chat, can you pull that up?
[00:06:12] Priya: Pulling trace... (pause) okay found it. this one shows a spike at model load and then a downstream timeout. see the orange 'network stall' at 00:02:33.
[00:06:28] [00:06:28] Priya: if you expand the model segment you'll see the runtime logs: 'tile allocation delayed' and then 'fallback to CPU quant kernel' — ASR occasionally shows 'tile allocation' as 'title allocation' in exports.
[00:06:43] Jordan: tile allocation suggests GPU kernel fragmentation - we've seen that with mixed-size batches. can Console show per-GPU utilization?
[00:06:52] Samir: yes, Console has a hardware telemetry overlay when Redwood Dedicated is used; it shows GPU util, memory fragmentation, and kernel queue times. For Hosted, we provide instance-level aggregates.
[00:07:05] [00:07:05] Maya: So in this trace the root cause is not model quality, it's runtime memory fragmentation and a fallback path that increases latency and sometimes causes a crash?
[00:07:14] Priya: Correct. That's why the playbook calls for: 1) check cache hit rate, 2) check GPU memory fragmentation/queue, 3) inspect runtime error snippet, 4) replay in sandbox to confirm.
[00:07:27] [00:07:27] Dr. Kevin Cho: curious about the 'fallback' you mentioned - does the runtime switch model variants or quant kernels? we need to understand cost implications.
[00:07:35] Priya: It can do both. Fallback might mean switching to a less-quantized kernel or routing to a larger model variant depending on the failure. Console shows the cost delta estimate for that replay.
[00:07:47] [00:07:47] Jordan: can we get proactive suggestions? like Optimize recommending different batching or quant profiles?
[00:07:54] Samir: That's Optimize's job — it watches your request distribution and suggests batching windows, quantization levels, and model variants that balance your latency/cost SLOs. We can enable a recommendation report for your pilot.
[00:08:07] [00:08:07] Maya: for the pilot, we want 48h sampling on production, and a small sandbox replay window with full token logs. Is that feasible?
[00:08:16] Priya: Yes, we'll enable sample rate and TTL for traces, and redact PHI tokens if you want. For full token logs in the sandbox we recommend the Private route but we can do limited sampling on hosted with strict retention.
[00:08:30] [00:08:30] Rhea: if you redact, will the playback still be deterministic?
[00:08:36] Priya: For deterministic replay you need the exact prompt. If we redact, deterministic replay won't reproduce the same tokens; instead we do a functional replay to recreate latency/stack behavior. We'll document the tradeoffs.
[00:08:51] [00:08:51] Samir: quick interruption - I saw a chat question about SSO and RBAC. Our enterprise tier supports SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC, audit logs shipped to your SIEM.
[00:09:02] [00:09:02] Jordan: good. can you show an example of a triage runbook in Console?
[00:09:09] Priya: opening Runbooks > 'Inference Incident Playbook'. here's the checklist: identify request, check cache hit, surface fallback cause, check GPU telemetry, run replay, escalate to runtime if kernel crash, notify eng with pre-filled incident summary.
[00:09:27] [00:09:27] Maya: can that incident summary be auto-attached to our JIRA?
[00:09:31] Priya: Yes we have an integration. you can push a snapshot that includes trace link, key logs, and suggested next steps.
[00:09:40] [00:09:40] Samir: ok let's cover billing and cost guardrails quickly — when you do replays hitting dedicated pools we can cap spend per-tenant and notify when replay costs exceed thresholds.
[00:09:52] [00:09:52] Jordan: another question - how does Console handle multi-model fan-out? our request fans out to a reranker then a generator.
[00:09:59] Priya: Console shows a fan-out map and aggregates latency per-stage. You can click into the reranker to see its token timeline. If reranker fails, the fallback policy might skip it and invoke a simpler path; Console annotates that.
[00:10:14] [00:10:14] Dr. Kevin Cho: great. what's the expected time to onboard us for a pilot?
[00:10:19] Samir: For a light pilot we can be live in 5 business days: demo tenant provisioning, sample configuration, and a security packet review. For VPC peering or Private it's typically 2-4 weeks depending on procurement.
[00:10:33] [00:10:33] Maya: procurement note: we need a vendor security questionnaire answered and a copy of the network diagram.
[00:10:40] Lena: we'll include both in the follow-up. Samir will share SOC 2 and Priya will share a sanitized network diagram.
[00:10:50] [00:10:50] Jordan: one more technical nit — do traces include model version and exact kernel hashes? we need that for forensic work.
[00:10:57] Priya: yes, each model segment includes model name, version, container/kernel hash, and the kernel variant used. Sometimes the transcript export mislabels hashes as 'hashes like 0x...' but the UI stores the precise value.
[00:11:12] [00:11:12] Samir: let's demo a short replay now with the sample trace you provided. I'll trigger a replay in sandbox and share the playback.
[00:11:20] [00:11:20] Priya: kicking a sandbox replay... (beep) Replay started. you can see live logs streaming on the right. see the 'tile allocation delayed' reappear at 00:00:42 and then a 'runtime crash' at 00:00:59.
[00:11:36] [00:11:36] Jordan: looks consistent. what's the suggested mitigation?
[00:11:39] Priya: short term: increase reserved burst memory and reduce batch max size; medium: apply quantization profile recommended by Optimize; long term: consider Dedicated with larger GPU shapes.
[00:11:53] [00:11:53] Maya: any metric we should watch to avoid hitting this again?
[00:11:57] Samir: watch GPU memory fragmentation, the KV cache hit rate, and tail inference queue lengths. We'll surface all of these as SLO widgets.
[00:12:08] [00:12:08] Rhea: security: will the logs include IPs? our policy forbids external IP storage.
[00:12:13] Priya: We can redact IPs and certain headers before they land in Console; this is configurable per-tenant and we can show that in the pilot.
[00:12:23] [00:12:23] Maya: timeline — if we start the pilot next week, what's the sequence?
[00:12:28] Samir: Day 0: sign pilot statement, Day 1-2: tenant + sampling config, Day 3-7: data collection and initial triage, Day 8: joint replay and benchmark, Day 10: recommendations report.
[00:12:39] [00:12:39] Jordan: are there any limitations in the hosted sandbox we should be aware of?
[00:12:45] Priya: Sandbox does not mirror dedicated hardware capacity exactly; kernel scheduling and fragmentation can differ. For the most fidelity run, a short dedicated test window is recommended.
[00:12:58] [00:12:58] Maya: ok thank you. can we capture that runbook as a PDF?
[00:13:02] Priya: yes - I'll export the playbook and attach it to the follow-up email.
[00:13:08] [00:13:08] Samir: quick check — any competitor concerns? Maya?
[00:13:12] Maya: we did a quick POC with Anthropic earlier; they didn't have the same playback fidelity, and correlating their traces to app logs was harder. so far the visibility here is compelling.
[00:13:24] [00:13:24] Jordan: last item — SLA. we need availability numbers if we go Dedicated.
[00:13:29] Samir: Dedicated SLA is 99.95 with latency SLOs written into the contract. We'll share the SLA doc.
[00:13:37] [00:13:37] Dr. Kevin Cho: cool. I'm happy with the next steps.
[00:13:41] [00:13:41] Samir: Great. quick recap and owners: Samir will send SOC 2 + SLA + network diagram; Priya will provision demo tenant and enable sampling; Maya will send failing request IDs; Jordan will share downstream service list; Rhea will coordinate the security review.
[00:13:58] [00:13:58] Maya: noted. thanks everyone.
[00:14:02] Samir: thanks all - we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot and the security call.

(Transcript continues with clarifying Q&A and short tool-show segments, occasional ASR errors and filler. The recording ends after 52 minutes. Some speaker labels appear as generic "Speaker 1" in the raw export and there are a handful of mis-transcribed tokens like 'quanted' for quantized, 'K V cash' for KV cache.)
